newsitem.title: UK: Rail watchdog mulls fines on Stagecoach unit.
newsitem.headline: Rail watchdog mulls fines on Stagecoach unit.

text.p: The UK Rail industry regulator said on Monday it was considering fining Stagecoach Plc's South West Trains unit after a sharp rise in train cancellations over the past week due to a driver shortage.

A spokesman for the Office of Passenger Rail Franchising (OPRAF) said performance targets were built into franchise agreements but that no decision would be taken on the possibility of fining Stagecoach or the size of such fines until it has analysed its performance for the rest of February.
"We will be analysing the data from this period and deciding what form of action is appropriate," said a spokesman for OPRAF.

"The company's performance to date has been very good, with reliability of 99.5 percent and punctuality of 92 percent...it is disappointing they are having this problem with drivers and we will have to look at the situation."
Shares in Stagecoach were down 4-1/2p at 720 by the close of business on Monday.
Stagecoach won the South West franchise, which runs services from London's Waterloo station through the south-west suburbs of London to Southampton, last December and began services on February 4.
It also holds the franchise to operate rail services on the Isle of Wight of the southern coast of England.
Reports said South West Trains would introduce an emergency timetable this week after a shortage of drivers led to the cancellation of some 17 services daily last week.

A spokeswoman for South West Trains said the company was having to cancel 39 out of a total of around 1500 daily services this week but had concentrated the cancellations on shorter services where other transport options were available.
